LLM auditresponse for .SRCINFO:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file defines metadata for the `gusco-bin` package, including sources and checksums for two architectures (x86_64 and aarch64). The sources point to official release binaries hosted on GitLab at `gitlab.com/intestinate/gusco`, which matches the project's stated URL (`https://intestinate.com/gusco/`). The SHA-256 checksums are explicitly provided for both binaries, ensuring integrity verification during package build. There is no executable code or script content in this file—only declarative packaging metadata.

The sources use the `::` syntax to rename the downloaded tarballs locally, which is standard AUR practice and does not affect security. Both download URLs are HTTPS-protected and hosted on the same domain as the project's official site. No checksums are marked as 'SKIP', and no network operations or file modifications are performed by this file. As a metadata-only file, `.SRCINFO` does not influence build behavior directly but reflects the content of the PKGBUILD.

This file presents no evidence of malicious behavior. It adheres to standard AUR packaging practices, uses verifiable checksums, and references only the official upstream release assets. While the use of a third-party GitLab instance (rather than self-hosting) could be considered a minor supply-chain consideration, GitLab is a trusted platform and the project's consistency across domains reduces risk.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD file fetches prebuilt binary releases of the gusco file manager from the official GitLab repository associated with the project (gitlab.com/intestinate/gusco). The sources are version-pinned (using `v${pkgver}`) and match the declared architecture (x86_64 or aarch64). Each architecture-specific source has a corresponding SHA-256 checksum, which is verified during package building. The package installs the binary to `/usr/bin`, documentation to `/usr/share/doc`, and the license file to `/usr/share/licenses`—all standard and expected locations.

No suspicious operations are present: there is no use of `eval`, no obfuscated code, no network requests outside the declared sources, and no unexpected file system modifications. The build process does not invoke compilers or build systems, which is appropriate for a `-bin` package distributing precompiled binaries. While the package skips stripping binaries (`!strip`), this is a common practice for some Go binaries and not inherently malicious. All actions align with standard AUR packaging practices for binary packages.

The upstream source is trusted (official project repository), and the integrity of the downloads is ensured via checksums. There is no evidence of supply chain tampering, backdoors, or data exfiltration.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
Standard binary package with verified checksums; no malicious activity detected</summary>

The URL appears to be the project's own upstream page, and the regex is used to parse version information from publicly available HTML. There are no network requests initiated within the file, no execution of external code, and no obfuscation. The use of `nvchecker` for automated version checks is a common and safe practice among AUR maintainers.

While the domain `intestinate.com` may appear unusual, the configuration itself does not exhibit malicious behavior. The file performs no actions on its own and requires a separate tool (`nvchecker`) to be run in a controlled context.
